::: {.why}
Corporate actions are where the identity of an instrument breaks, and an identifier that changes without warning is the bug that corrupts a universe silently for years.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- For each of split, cash dividend, spinoff and ticker change, say what happens to the price series and what happens to the identifier.
- Explain why a ticker is not a primary key, and name what is used instead.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Work through your three saved corporate actions in a notebook. For each, plot the raw series across the event, state the adjustment factor, and say whether a naive returns calculation would have produced a spurious return and of what size.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [20 min]{.task-min} The identifier problem: write down what happens to a ticker when a company is acquired, when it changes name, and when a different company later takes the freed ticker. Then write the one-line rule your data store will follow, which is that the primary key is an internal integer and the ticker is an attribute with valid-from and valid-to dates.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Add the spinoff case to the glossary, since it is the one that most often goes unhandled: the parent's price drops by the value of what was distributed, and the holder received shares rather than cash.
:::
:::
